mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% within the prior 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces earnings and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a double-hit to demand, amplifying recession risk and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of dual-triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recessionary regime signals aggressive monetary easing, which boosts equity valuations via lower discount rates and improved growth expectations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 3.0% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of easing episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month coincident with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE change near zero) signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1% MoM AND |UNRATE change| < 0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.
